newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-TWO GRAND SLAMS POWER PHILLIES PAST GIANTS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-TWO GRAND SLAMS POWER PHILLIES PAST GIANTS.

text.p: Billy McMillon and Mike Lieberthal each hit their first career grand slam on Monday to power the red-hot Philadelphia Phillies to a 12-3 victory over the San Francisco Giants.
The two grand slams tied a team record dating back to 1921, when Ralph Miller and Lee Meadows accomplished the feat against the Boston Braves.

McMillon, who was acquired from the Florida Marlins last month and recalled from the minors earlier Monday, had three hits and made his first major league homer a memorable one in his Philadelphia debut.
His grand slam off San Francisco starter Mark Gardner (12-7) with two outs in the third inning, staked the Phillies to a 4-0 lead.
"I feel like I need to wake up and roll over," said McMillon of his blast over the wall in right with the bases loaded.
"It's like a dream. I never thought I would do it. I felt like I was running around the bases too fast. But I didn't know how to act because it was my first homer in the majors."
Lieberthal's 18th home run of the season in the sixth inning off former Phillie Terry Mulholland provided Philadelphia with a 10-2 advantage.

Matt Beech (2-7) posted his second straight victory after going winless in his first 14 starts of the season. The left-hander allowed two runs -- one earned -- and three hits over seven innings with two walks and five strikeouts.
Mickey Morandini and Rico Brogna each had three hits for Philadelphia, which won for the 11th time in 14 games.
"We didn't play good baseball tonight," San Francisco manager Dusty Baker said. "It's tough to win when you give up two grand slams and make four errors."
At Florida, Esteban Loaiza allowed one earned run over six innings and Dale Sveum added a homer and three RBI as the Pittsburgh Pirates beat the Marlins 7-2 to gain a split of a four-game series.
Loaiza (9-8) allowed seven hits, walking one and striking out three. The right-hander allowed a homer to Moises Alou in the fourth but held the Marlins in check after that.

Sveum drove in a run in the seventh, an inning in which the Pirates took advantage of a pair of Florida errors to score three times and take a 5-2 lead. He added a two-run homer in the ninth off Marlins closer Robb Nen.

Jermaine Allensworth had three hits, including his third homer, scored twice and drove in a pair of runs and Eddie Williams added three hits, including a pair of doubles, for the Pirates, who beat former manager Jim Leyland.

Florida's Kirt Ojala made his major-league but lasted just 3 2/3 innings, allowing two runs and four hits while walking three as the Marlins saw their lead over the New York Mets in the National League wild-card race shrink to four games.
